correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the permutation-equivariant table count as n^{-N} times the product of fixed points of powers of each permutation over its unordered-pair orbits. A transposition has exactly binom(n-2,2)+1 fixed pair positions and n-2 two-cycle pair-orbits, hence probability p_n. For support k>=3 the pair-orbit deficit is at least k(2n-k-2)/4; splitting k<=n/2 and k>n/2 gives a convergent B_n bound. Outside this exceptional event, the automorphism group is trivial or generated by one transposition, so the expected transposition count and existence probability differ by at most (1+binom(n,2))B_n. The B_n-to-main-term ratio vanishes, and Taylor expansion fixes e^4/2. Burnside then gives the stated first correction. Direct exhaustive table checks cover n=3,4; permutation orbit/formula checks cover n<=7 and do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The central natural problem is the rate at which random commutative-idempotent operations acquire nonidentity automorphisms. Previously qualitative asymmetry leaves the rare-event rate and typical exceptional stabilizer unknown. The precise e^{-n}n^{4-n} leading law, deterministic support suppression, and conditional classification as a single transposition are structurally informative, and they also yield the first correction to unlabeled Burnside enumeration. These claims are not routine restatements of known finite counts and are stable across the infinite family.
